On the owner's live backend (139 patches) on 2026-10-11: GET /api/schedule -> 200, jobs: 1, todo: 0, went_off: 1, running: true, ids se80955f188 and s1106891920; then POST /api/schedule/act with {"id": "s1106891920", "do": "delete"} and the usual X-Jarvis-Token / X-Jarvis-Client: hud -> 404 {"ok": false, "reason": "no_such_job", "error": "That is not on the list any more."}. So the PC lists that job under went_off and then rejects it as not on the list: a fired entry cannot be cleared until it ages out of went_off an hour later, and the phone shows it that whole time. WHERE THE TWO SIDES DIFFER, both in backend/jarvis_schedule.py (jarvis-backend/jarvis_schedule.py is byte-identical, same lines): the READ puts a fired job in went_off - handle_get:2037 answers with status(), status():1834 sets "went_off": self.went_off(now), and went_off()'s query at :1413-1417 accepts state IN ('fired','active','paused') within WENT_OFF_SHOWN = 3600.0 (:189 - one hour, documented at docs/JARVIS-API.md:4740); the WRITE refuses it - the route at backend/schedule.patch:82 calls jarvis_schedule.handle_act(body), handle_act:2158 calls get().act(jid, do, seconds), and act()'s gate at :1271-1274 accepts only state IN ('active','paused','waiting'), the same set the live list uses at :1805-1806, so anything 'fired' comes back 404 no_such_job. The SAME route, same id, accepts snooze: act() routes do == "snooze" to snooze() at :1267, and snooze()'s own gate at :1380 accepts state IN ('fired','active','paused') within FIRED_KEEP (24 hours); GET /api/schedule?id=<id> answers 200 for it too (handle_get:2032-2036, via job():1797-1800, which has no state filter). THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS: went_off may legitimately be history rather than a job, so "not on the list any more" is an honest sentence - the finding is the INCONSISTENCY between the two routes, not that either side is obviously wrong. docs/JARVIS-API.md:5058-5061 documents the two windows as deliberately different ("The route reaches back a day ... while the Just went off list and the spoken phrase reach back one hour"), and snooze is the verb that implements the day-long reach-back. THIS IS NOT THE CAUSE OF THE ALARM THAT RANG FOR EVER (that one is DEF-006): that incident happened with the jobs ABSENT FROM ALL THREE LISTS (went_off empty, more than an hour after they fired) - exactly the condition the phone's reconcile now covers. The notification side is already covered by #280: the reconcile needs the job absent from jobs + todo + went_off and does NOT need the delete to succeed, so nothing is unfixed for the owner's original complaint. If the owner wants a way to clear a fired entry, that is a PRODUCT DECISION - a "Clear this" on the went-off row - not a bug fix. Do not repair it here or anywhere yet.
